title: More weight doesn’t always mean more stimulation.
hook: More weight doesn’t always mean more stimulation.
caption:
More weight doesn’t always mean more stimulation.

If your goal is to increase the size of a specific muscle for aesthetic purposes—not simply to become stronger or move more weight—the amount of weight lifted is only part of the equation.

A heavier weight may allow you to move more load from point A to point B, but it can also cause surrounding muscles to take over more of the work. This creates greater muscular synergy, but it may reduce how much of the stimulus reaches the specific muscle you’re trying to grow.
